NGA.note: Editorial mentions NIN verification in general; no authentication service described.
Nothing on a link to civil registration.
Nothing on digital finance consumer protection.
Only says the NIMC Act has stronger data protection; an identity law is not the general data protection law.

facts.fact: A Leadership editorial says presidential assent to the National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 repealed the 2007 legislation and that Nigeria is moving to strict statutory enforcement of the NIN across banking, telecoms and social safety nets.

The editorial describes the NIMC Act 2026 as setting a framework for unified national identity governance and database interoperability across ministries and agencies, with the NIN as the cornerstone of civic verification and biometric tracking.

NGA.note: Fertiliser subsidies and loans mentioned only as services needing NIN; no digital payment stated.
Says millions are undocumented but gives no count or share.
Nothing on a number at birth.
Nothing on who operates or owns the system.
Interoperability across agencies is said of the Act in general; no register named as keyed on the NIN.

facts.fact: A Leadership editorial describes enrolment centres across the country operating the NIN and the NIMC database, where people pay fees to correct records.

systems.system: National Identification Number (NIN) and NIMC database

NGA.note: Nothing on local government office connection.
Only calls for enrolment in IDP camps; the Act's provisions for underserved groups are not described as delivered.
Nothing on mobile money or retail payments.
Social safety nets named only as needing NIN; no programme system stated.
